newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana bourse rebounds, key bank shares recover.
newsitem.headline: Ghana bourse rebounds, key bank shares recover.

text.p: The Ghana Stock Exchange All-Share Index rebounded on Friday, boosted by renewed interest in Ghana Commercial Bank GCB.GH, brokers said.
The Index rose 5.62 points from 349.67 points to 355.29 points -- up on the prvious week's close of 354.01 points.
Ghana Commercial Bank GCB.GH, which shed 40 cedis on Wednesday on a scandal over unauthorised lending, gained 50 cedis to end the week at 650 cedis.
Would-be buyers outnumbered sellers with 2,449,520 shares bid against 936,920 shares offered. A total of 89,120 shares changed hands.
Brokers said the bulk of interest -- 2,000,900 offers -- came from foreign institutional buyers attracted by Pioneer Tobacco Company. There were no sellers.
Enterprise Insurance Company (+2 cedis to 472 cedis) was the only other mover.

Ghana Commercial Bank fell on Wednesday after the finance ministry announced that its managing director Helen Lokko retired over the scandal involving 70 billion cedis of unauthorised lending to a supermarket chain.
In March last year, Ghana Commercial Bank went public and sold 42 percent of shares, while the sale of only 30 percent had been initially envisaged.

Last November, the Denko Industrial Corp Berhad of Malaysia acquired a 40 percent stake in the bank. The Malaysians are expected to take over the management as soon as the deal is ratified by Ghana's president, Jerry Rawlings.
